findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that the idle-sync loop catches unexpected exceptions from idle_sync, logs them at WARNING, and continues on the next interval so a transient error does not permanently kill the background sync thread.
evidence: Plan: 'A daemon thread ... runs a new sync.idle_sync(tracker) every 120 s'
idle_sync adds push/fetch failure points; plan specifies logging only for PUSH_PENDING/DIVERGED/lock-skipped outcomes, not for an uncaught exception terminating the loop
ABSENCE: no statement that the loop catches and logs unexpected exceptions and continues to the next interval
findings.finding: The idle-sync daemon thread's resilience to an unexpected exception inside idle_sync is unspecified. If idle_sync raises (not a push rejection, but e.g. an fs/network error during reconverge), the plan does not say the thread survives and retries on the next 120 s tick. A dying daemon thread silently stops all background syncs, recreating the original 'Nothing pushed the fork until a client wrote' failure mode.
scenarios: reconverge hits a transient fetch/IO error that is not a classified push outcome; the daemon thread's run loop propagates and the thread exits; no further idle syncs run for the container's lifetime, silently

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the rollback path for steps 1-2 (e.g. revert the Gerrit change / redeploy prior image) and confirm it needs no data cleanup, since the idle_sync timer has no runtime kill switch by design.
evidence: 'The interval is a module constant: no new config key, env var, or lock.'
'the handler waits, within the existing grace, for that worker to exit and the store write lock to be free, then sets should_exit'
ABSENCE: no rollback/disable path stated for the new retirement-wait or idle_sync behavior
findings.finding: The plan changes runtime behavior of a long-running deployed MCP server (SIGTERM retirement sequence, an always-on 120s idle_sync daemon, default-level logging) but states no rollback path. The idle_sync timer is deliberately unconditional ('no new config key, env var, or lock'), so if the new retirement wait or sync loop misbehaves in production there is no cheap toggle or documented revert to disable it quickly.
findings.location: Approach steps 1-2; Scope ('The interval is a module constant: no new config key, env var, or lock.')
scenarios: If the new SIGTERM wait hangs retirement or idle_sync's push loop causes contention in prod, operators have no flag to disable it and must redeploy a reverted image.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line rollback statement: each of the 3 changes is independently revertable via Gerrit; reverting change (1)/(2+3) restores prior SIGTERM/sync behavior with no on-disk state to clean up.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State, per idle_sync failure arm, its disposition: PUSH_PENDING/lock-skipped are retryable on the next 120s cycle; specify whether DIVERGED is retryable or needs-investigation, and whether a reconverge lock-skip still retries push.
evidence: 'idle_sync logs at WARNING when a run ends PUSH_PENDING (with its reason, such as non-fast-forward), DIVERGED, or lock-skipped (naming the holder)'
'a busy lock silently skips reconverge'
ABSENCE: no disposition word (retryable/transient vs fatal/permanent) attached to DIVERGED or to the reconverge-skip + push composition
findings.finding: Step 2/3 add/alter a push failure path (reconverge then push) whose outcomes are logged (PUSH_PENDING, DIVERGED, lock-skipped) but the plan never states the DISPOSITION per arm — whether DIVERGED is retryable on the next 120s cycle or needs operator investigation, and whether a reconverge lock-skip still leaves HEAD-ahead push to retry. The composition (reconverge arm + push arm) has no stated winner when reconverge is skipped.
findings.location: Approach step 2 ('idle_sync calls reconverge ... then calls push.push_after_commit ...') and step 3 (WARNING on PUSH_PENDING/DIVERGED/lock-skipped)
scenarios: A DIVERGED idle_sync run logs WARNING but the plan does not say whether the next 120s tick retries or whether divergence is terminal until an operator acts.
A busy-lock skip of reconverge: the plan does not say whether push still attempts (masking a stale HEAD) or whether the whole run is retryable next cycle.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a one-line positive rationale to Approach step 2 for the periodic idle-timer (why a 120s background poll, holding the gauge and skipping on lock contention, is the right fit for publishing an un-pushed fork absent a client write) rather than only naming the mechanism.
evidence: Plan: 'A daemon thread ... runs a new sync.idle_sync(tracker) every 120 s'

reconverge (src/rebar/_store/sync.py:224) 'fetches and merges but never pushes' — the plan names this gap but gives no positive rationale for a timer vs. a push-pending-marker drain on the existing reconverge/write paths
ABSENCE: steps 1 and 4 carry positive 'why this fits' rationale; step 2 states only the mechanism and interval
findings.finding: Approach step 2 specifies the idle-timer sync mechanism (a 120s daemon poll calling reconverge then push_after_commit) but states no POSITIVE rationale for choosing a periodic background poll over structurally-different alternatives — e.g. draining a push-pending marker at the point of reconverge, or pushing on the retirement/SIGTERM path alongside the end-of-run sweep push. The chosen approach is defensible (reconverge already never pushes; a timer is the smallest independent addition that publishes a fork absent a client write), but the plan should say WHY the poll fits so the implementer does not re-litigate the interval/trigger choice.
scenarios: Implementer or reviewer questions why 120s / why a poll rather than coupling the push to the already-planned SIGTERM worker-exit path
